t:
(a) 
Authority.—
        (1) 
In addition to funds otherwise available for such purpose, the Secretary of the Army may transfer or reprogram funds for the enhancement of the capabilities of the Bad Aibling Station and the Menwith Hill Station, including improvements of facility infrastructure and quality of life programs at those installations.
 
        (2) 
The authority of paragraph (1) may be exercised notwithstanding any other provision of law.
  
    (b) 
Source of Funds.—Funds available for the Army for operations and maintenance for fiscal years 1996 and 1997 shall be available to carry out subsection (a).
 
    (c) 
Congressional Notification.—Whenever the Secretary of the Army determines that an amount to be transferred or reprogrammed under this section would cause the total amount transferred or reprogrammed in that fiscal year under this section to exceed $1,000,000, the Secretary shall notify in advance the Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on National Security, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and provide a justification for the increased expenditure.
 
    (d) 
Statutory Construction.—Nothing in this section may be construed to modify or obviate existing law or practice with regard to the transfer or reprogramming of funds in excess of $2,000,000 from the Department of the Army to the Bad Aibling Station and the Menwith Hill Station.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the advance notification and justification requirement is a form of consultation before a federal decision. But the only parties notified are congressional committees, which are inside the federal government, so the process never crosses the federal boundary. The rest of the section only authorizes the Secretary of the Army to transfer or reprogram funds, with no public comment, rulemaking, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary shall notify in advance the Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Army to notify various congressional committees. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so this notification is an intra-governmental action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary shall notify in advance the Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on National Security, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives

opus.w: The only procedural requirement is advance notice and a justification sent to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. Notices to Congress are a listed trap, not participation. Nothing in the section has the Secretary consult outside parties, hold a hearing, take public comment or allow anyone to sue before deciding to transfer funds.
opus.s: the Secretary shall notify in advance the Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on National Security, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and provide a justification for the increased expenditure.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that subsection (c) counts as participation, because the Secretary must notify congressional committees in advance and justify transfers over $1,000,000. That fails the definition: Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so this is an internal notice, not outside participation. The rest of the section only covers transfer authority, where the money comes from, and how the section should be read. It involves no states, members of the public, experts or other outside parties, and gives no one a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Army to notify various congressional committees before transferring funds. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Notification to internal government bodies does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary shall notify in advance the Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on National Security, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves communication with an external body before a decision is finalized. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to or notifying Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
